seo.title: Teradata client for {devices}
seo.description: Log on to Teradata Vantage with TD2 or TDNEGO, over a plain session or TLS, browse databases, users, procedures and macros, and create and alter tables.

header.title: Teradata client for {devices}
header.lead: Log on with TD2 or TDNEGO, browse databases and users with their tables, views, procedures and macros, and query and edit through a native Swift driver, with no Teradata client software to install.

sections.title: Connect and log on
paragraphs: Enter the host, username and password. Any Vantage system that accepts a TD2 logon works, and no version is checked. Logon Mechanism in the Options section takes TD2 or TDNEGO, and Database is needed only for a default other than your account’s.

The default port carries a plain session. Any SSL mode moves the session to the gateway’s WebSocket endpoint on port 443, which cannot be changed. Verify CA needs a CA certificate, and Verify Identity checks the chain and hostname against that certificate or, without one, the system trust store.

Leave Transaction Mode on DEFAULT unless a script needs ANSI or TERA commit rules and case sensitivity on the session. Reach a system behind a bastion through an SSH tunnel. Import from URL… accepts teradata:// URLs, which macOS does not open as links.

sections.title: Query and edit
paragraphs: A database and a user are both namespaces in Teradata, so both appear at the top of the sidebar with their tables and views. A tab bound to a second database keeps the same session and runs DATABASE ahead of its statements.
Stored procedures are listed in the sidebar, and macros sit under Functions, each opening its <objects>source in a read-only tab</objects>.

Teradata has no LIMIT, so a table’s first page comes back with TOP and later pages with QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER(). EXPLAIN returns Teradata’s plan as raw text. Row edits wait until you save, and Preview SQL shows each statement first.

sections.title: Structure
paragraphs: Create tables and change their columns from the <structure>Structure tab</structure>. A table’s DDL view shows its full definition, constraints included.

sections.title: Move data
paragraphs: Bring {importFormats} files in with <importData>Import</importData>, and save a table or a result as {exportFormats}. <copy>Copy To</copy> sends tables, their rows or both to another Teradata connection; a copy to a different engine is refused.

faq.question: Why is my logon mechanism ignored?
faq.answer: Type it in uppercase. A value the driver does not recognise, such as a lowercase tdnego, is read as TD2.

faq.question: How do I know the session is encrypted?
faq.answer: Test with Required (skip verify) or a verify mode. Preferred falls back to a plain session when the TLS port is unreachable, so with it a failed handshake still looks like a successful connect.
